question.summary: Known examples are consistent with the proposed completely bounded entropy or coherent-information conditions, but no theorem covers every multiplicativity counterexample.
question.importance: A universal entropy signature would explain why known output-norm counterexamples work and connect multiplicativity failure to coherent information.
question.unresolved: Prove the requested CB-entropy or coherent-information structure for all maximal-output-norm counterexamples, or give a counterexample to that structure.

formulation.notation:
| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $M_d$ | algebra of $d\times d$ complex matrices |
| $\Phi$ | quantum channel (CPT map) |
| $\Phi^C$ | complementary channel of $\Phi$ |
| $S(\rho)$ | von Neumann entropy of state $\rho$, $S(\rho)=-\operatorname{Tr}\rho\log\rho$ |
| $S^p(\rho)$ | Renyi $p$-entropy, $\tfrac{1}{p-1}\log\operatorname{Tr}\rho^p$ for $p\ne 1$ |
| $I_{\rm coh}(\rho,\Phi)$ | coherent information, $I_{\rm coh}(\rho,\Phi)=S[\Phi(\rho)]-S[\Phi^C(\rho)]$ |
| $S_{\rm CB}(\Phi)$ | completely-bounded (CB) entropy of the channel $\Phi$, as defined in Devetak-Junge-King-Ruskai (CMP 266, 2006) |
| EB | entanglement-breaking channel |
| WH | Werner-Holevo channel (Werner-Holevo 2002) |
| eq. (24) | multiplicativity assertion $\nu_p(\Phi\otimes\Omega)=\nu_p(\Phi)\nu_p(\Omega)$ |
formulation.statement:
**Problem 21 (Ruskai 2007).** Do *all* counter-examples to multiplicativity (24) of the maximal output $p$-norm have non-negative CB entropy and/or zero (i.e. non-positive at the violating input) coherent information?

Equivalently: does every quantum channel $\Phi$ for which there exists $\Omega$ and $p

progress.title: Completely bounded norms give forward additivity implications
progress.detail: Devetak, Junge, King and Ruskai establish the foundational CB-norm connection, but not the converse classification requested here.
progress.label: CB-norm framework

evidence.interpretation: A statement that coherent information is zero must specify whether this is an input value, the channel maximum, or a capacity.
